extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of political philosophy (founders of a State, guardians' educators)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for founding and educating the guardian class in an ideal city (division of labour, moral and artistic censorship, selection of natures, and training in courage and temperance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labour (one craft per person)
rubrics_metrics.description: One man cannot practise many arts with success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each person should be assigned one work for which he is by nature fitted and continue in it all his life, so that he becomes a good workman; e.g. the shoemaker must not also be a husbandman or builder. This principle grounds the social structure and the assignment of roles including soldiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish marketplace and money for exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: They will need a market-place, and a money-token for purposes of exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A monetary medium creates classes of retail-traders and merchants; those weak in bodily strength may be put to market duties so producers need not abandon their crafts to find buyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and role of retail-traders and hirelings
rubrics_metrics.description: A want for exchange creates a class of retail-traders and another class of servants who sell bodily labour (hirelings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retailers sit in the marketplace buying and selling; hirelings supply labour. These social roles arise naturally from economic needs and must be acknowledged when framing the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject unlimited luxury expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: The original healthy State is sufficient for necessities; adding luxuries (sofas, tables, dainties, perfumes, courtesans, gold and ivory) creates many unnecessary callings and leads to enlargement of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A luxurious State requires many non-natural occupations (poets, painters, embroiderers, tutors, cooks, etc.), leads to greater resource needs, and precipitates expansionist pressures and war.

rubrics_metrics.name: War arises from excessive accumulation and desire for more land
rubrics_metrics.description: If people exceed the limit of necessity and give themselves up to the unlimited accumulation of wealth we shall want a slice of our neighbours' land and so go to war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: War is linked to causes of evils in States; recognizing its origins in appetite/expansion is important before judging whether war does good or harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: War and soldiering require specialization and training
rubrics_metrics.description: War is an art; an art requiring as much attention as shoemaking — nothing will make a man a skilled workman or master of defence who has not learned how to handle the tools and bestowed attention upon them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guardian cannot be effective if he is also a husbandman or artisan; guardians must devote early and continuous training to their craft (military art) to be competent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select natural aptitudes for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be our duty to select, if we can, natures which are fitted for the task of guarding the city.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is difficult but necessary; guardians should be chosen for bodily strength, spirit, swiftness, and natural aptitude for guarding duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bodily qualities required of guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians ought to be quick to see, swift to overtake the enemy when they see him, and strong too if, when they have caught him, they have to fight with him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical physical requirements include sight, speed, and strength — the tools which would teach men their own use would be beyond price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spirited character (thumos) and bravery
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardian's soul is to be full of spirit; he must be brave if he is to fight well; spirit makes the soul fearless and indomitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians must possess spirit/natural courage; without spirit they cannot be brave. But spirit must be balanced (see gentleness criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentleness to friends and fierceness to enemies (harmonized opposites)
rubrics_metrics.description: They ought to be dangerous to their enemies, and gentle to their friends; otherwise they will destroy themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although spirit can incline to savagery, guardians must combine spiritedness with gentleness toward acquaintances — a difficult but attainable combination (examples drawn from well-bred dogs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophic love of learning as a guardian trait
rubrics_metrics.description: He who is likely to be gentle to his friends and acquaintances must by nature be a lover of wisdom and knowledge; the love of learning (philosophy) distinguishes friend from enemy by knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians should combine philosophy with spirit, swiftness and strength — the truly good guardian unites these traits; education must cultivate love of wisdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin education with music (literature) before gymnastics
rubrics_metrics.description: Education has two divisions, gymnastic for the body, and music for the soul; we shall begin by telling children stories and teaching music before gymnastics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The beginning is the most important part; early tales form character more readily than gymnastics molds the body, so narrative and literary content must be carefully controlled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censorship of fiction and authorised tales for children
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a censorship of the writers of fiction: censors receive any tale of fiction which is good, and reject the bad; mothers and nurses should tell their children the authorised ones only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow casual tales that give opposite ideas to those desired in grown guardians; authors/fabricators of tales must be limited to forms and limits set by the founders of the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of gods: God as cause of good only
rubrics_metrics.description: God is always to be represented as he truly is; God, if he be good, is not the author of all things but of good only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poets must not say that gods are authors of evil or that divine action mixes good and evil; attributing evil to gods is 'suicidal, ruinous, impious' and must be forbidden in well-ordered commonwealths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of gods: immutable and non-deceptive
rubrics_metrics.description: The gods are not magicians who transform themselves; being fairest and best, every God remains absolutely and for ever in his own form; the superhuman and divine is absolutely incapable of falsehood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No poet should depict gods as changing shapes, deceiving, or using phantoms; such representations make children fearful, misled, or morally confused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit tales that justify quarrelling or impious behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not tell children stories which represent quarrelling among gods and heroes as acceptable or which show gods stealing, deceiving, or instigating human wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tales like the wars in heaven, plots of gods, or Cronus's deeds should be buried or reserved for very few in mystery; early tales should be models of virtuous thoughts so youth learn that quarrelling is unholy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppress terrifying depictions of the underworld
rubrics_metrics.description: Expunge passages that describe the world below with horrific names and images (Cocytus, Styx, ghosts, sapless shades) which make the guardians fear death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such graphic portrayals render guardians' nerves too excitable and effeminate; instead compose a nobler strain that presents death as not terrible to the good man.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid excessive lamentation and public weeping among guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Get rid of the weepings and wailings of famous men; the good man will not consider death terrible and will bear misfortune with equanimity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lamentation should be assigned to women or lower sorts so guardians scorn excessive mourning and maintain composure; portrayals of heroes' frantic grief are to be excised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid portrayals of excessive laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither ought our guardians to be given to laughter; a fit of laughter indulged to excess produces a violent reaction and persons of worth must not be represented as overcome by laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid representations (even of gods) in inextinguishable laughter; guardians should not be taught to emulate such behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and regulated lying (noble lie for rulers only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth should be highly valued; the lie in words is useful only as medicine in certain cases, and if anyone is to have the privilege of lying the rulers of the State should be the persons — lying is allowed for the public good but forbidden to private individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers may lie to enemies or to citizens for public benefit; any other person (craftsmen, priests, physicians, carpenters) who lies shall be punished for undermining the State. Lying by subordinates to rulers is a more heinous fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate temperance (obedience and self-control)
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief elements of temperance are obedience to commanders and self-control in sensual pleasures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approve language and stories that promote obedience and restrained behaviour; avoid popular impertinences and verses that glorify drinking, gift-seeking, or appetite-driven conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid encouraging love of money or gift-seeking
rubrics_metrics.description: Youth must not be receivers of gifts or lovers of money; do not sing to them of 'gifts persuading gods, and persuading reverend kings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject tales that teach pupils to take gifts in lieu of duty (example: Phoenix's counsel to Achilles); moral education must remove incentive structures that corrupt guardians' motivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate to be fearless of death
rubrics_metrics.description: Can any man be courageous who has the fear of death in him? We must control narrators to extirpate descriptions which make the world below seem real and terrible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrayals that make death seem frightful will prevent soldiers from choosing death in battle rather than defeat; educational censorship should ensure guardians are not taught to fear death.
